captions.instagram:
How is tea made?

Green tea and black tea are the same leaf. Crush it and an enzyme turns it copper in an hour; heat it first and it stays green. Run the factory, stop the oxidation at the right minute, then brew it: caffeine rushes out first, the bitter tannins keep coming, and a pan of chai shows why milk makes it smooth.

→ Every tea starts the same way: two leaves and a bud from one plant, Camellia sinensis.
→ Inside each cell, bitter catechins and an enzyme are kept apart. Crush the leaf and they meet oxygen: green turns copper.
→ In the factory, withered leaf meets CTC rollers: crush, tear, curl. Invented in Assam in 1930, they make most of India's tea.
→ Then the torn leaf oxidises: green turns copper. Stop too early and the tea is raw, too late and it is dull.
→ Green, oolong and black tea are the same leaf. The only question is how long it oxidises before heat stops the enzyme.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/teaclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How is tea made? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Green tea and black tea are the same leaf. Crush it and an enzyme turns it copper in an hour; heat it first and it stays green. Run the factory, stop the oxidation at the right minute, then brew it: caffeine rushes out first, the bitter tannins keep coming, and a pan of chai shows why milk makes it smooth.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/teaclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/teaclear

In this video:
• One plant, kept in two rooms. All tea comes from Camellia sinensis.
• The factory breaks the wall. The leaf is withered from about 77% water to about 70%, then rolled or cut by CTC rollers so the cells tear.
• Six teas from one leaf. Heat the leaf first and the enzyme dies: green tea.
• The brew is a race. Caffeine is small and leaves the leaf fast: half is out of whole black leaf in under two minutes at 80 °C (measured).
• Why chai is boiled with milk. CTC granules in boiling water give up nearly all their caffeine within a minute and their tannins soon after.
• India's cup, and yours. India made about 1,285 million kg of tea in 2024, half of it in Assam, and drinks about four fifths of it.
